topics.label: Introduction and lecture framing
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the introductory framing and context for the lecture on complement.

topics.label: Overview and core mechanics of complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce the fundamental architecture, nomenclature conventions, and the central role of C3 activation in the complement cascade.

topics.label: Pathways of complement activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the three upstream recognition mechanisms that drive the assembly of surface convertases to activate complement on pathogens.

topics.label: Downstream effector mechanisms of complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the three major effector outcomes triggered by complement activation to destroy pathogens and stimulate inflammation.

topics.label: Host regulation and self-protection mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how regulatory proteins prevent inappropriate complement activation and protect host cells from damage.

topics.label: Clinical consequences of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines how genetic or acquired deficiencies across different complement proteins lead to distinct clinical disease presentations.

topics.label: Pathogen strategies for evading complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic describes the specialized mechanisms evolved by pathogens to resist complement recognition and destruction.

topics.label: Closing remarks and next lecture preview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the concluding framing and housekeeping for the lecture.
